verdict.rationale: First-party material says Cloudflare bills CPU compute rather than wall time during long agent workflows, and that Workflows can persist state for minutes, hours or weeks. The only concrete limits (30s CPU on free, 15min on paid) come from a community comment, not official docs. missing for 10: first-party documented CPU-time limits per plan, documented wall-clock/duration limits for Workers requests and cron triggers, independent corroboration of the limit values

support.subject: As a devops-lead, I know the CPU and wall-clock execution time limits for functions so I can tell whether long-running or agentic workloads will fit

citations.quote: Cloudflare charges only for compute, not wall time, even during long agent workflows or hibernating WebSockets.
persist state for minutes, hours, or even weeks - with no infrastructure to manage
The 30s CPU time on the free tier and even the 15min on paid plans don't work for long-running agent tasks.
